races.name: Why Settle Technology AI Adoption EBF Maiden Stakes (Hamilton 2yo Series Qualifier) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Pikachu
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's 106-rated runner has four outings over 7f on Good ground but now steps up to 1m½f on softer footing, a significant shift that could flatter or expose stamina limits; Egan takes over and the lone front-runner role hands him full control of the race, though racing at a trip 3.5f longer than any previous start is the key unknown.

runners_data.name: Trumpety Trump
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's hold-up type has placed in both career runs over 6f on Good, and the step to 1m½f on Good to Soft represents an ambitious extension; drawn into the hunter's position naturally, Trumpety Trump needs Pikachu to crack and the longer trip to bring stamina into play to have any realistic chance.

runners_data.name: Nice Neasy Does It
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's debutant carries the highest rating at OR 120 and an intriguing unknown profile — going and running style both flagged as uncertain — making it the wild card of the race; David Allan is a shrewd northern jockey who knows this track and Easterby debutants on softer ground can be well-schooled at home, so the absence of form cuts both ways.

races.paceDynamic: Pikachu is the lone confirmed pace-setter in this three-runner maiden and will stride to the front from the outset, setting a controlled, uncontested tempo over 1m½f on Good to Soft ground. With Trumpety Trump a hold-up type and Nice Neasy Does It essentially unknown in running style, nothing will pressure Pikachu in the early stages, meaning the fractions will be dictated entirely by David Egan's judgement. That unchallenged, metronomic lead on a stamina-testing Hamilton trip in soft-ish ground is a classic recipe for a front-runner to control the race throughout and simply gallop rivals into submission. This shape strongly favours a prominent or front-running profile — the horse who leads can conserve energy through the bends and have first run into the straight, leaving hold-up types with ground to make up on a track that does not favour flat-out late charges.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pikachu Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Pikachu bowls along uncontested and David Egan manages the pace to leave enough in reserve for the home straight.
scenarios.body: Pikachu takes a comfortable lead, dictates soft fractions that suit a galloping 2yo, and the longer trip on Good to Soft rewards stamina over raw speed — hold-up rivals have no signal to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Pikachu goes too fast for conditions, tying itself up in the final furlong and gifting a closer the race.
scenarios.body: The strong early gallop drains Pikachu's reserves on energy-sapping ground, allowing a hold-up or prominent type to mow it down in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Newcomer Stuns Field
scenarios.trigger: If Nice Neasy Does It arrives with significant home gallop form and takes to the track immediately under David Allan.
scenarios.body: An Easterby-trained debutant on familiar northern ground can spring a surprise, particularly if unknown ability translates well over the stamina test at this trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Muddle No Winner
scenarios.trigger: If jockeys misjudge the pace dramatically and all three runners hit the line in a flat, tired finish.
scenarios.body: With only three runners and no benchmark pace, a catastrophic misjudgement could compress the finish, but this remains highly unlikely given Pikachu's clear role as the natural pace horse.

watchPoints.text: Watch Pikachu's sectionals in the first half-mile — if David Egan allows even a modest increase in tempo on this testing ground, the extra 3.5f beyond Pikachu's form trip could cause it to empty dramatically inside the final furlong.

Nice Neasy Does It is a complete unknown and Tim Easterby has a notably low 14-day win rate (5/84); monitor market movement closely as a well-backed debutant here would significantly shift the probability landscape.

Trumpety Trump has only raced over 6f on Good ground; the combination of a stamina step-up of nine furlongs and softer conditions than anything in its form record means it may simply lack the raw engine to close the gap on a controlling leader.

With just three runners, any early incident such as a slow break by Pikachu or crowding at the first bend could completely restructure the pace shape and open the door for Nice Neasy Does It to assume a position it was never expected to occupy.

races.name: Huws Gray British Stallions EBF Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Krissy
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner who will bowl clear from the gates; her record shows just one win and no places from 15 runs on similar going, which is a significant stamina and form concern over this trip, though her tactical role as pace-setter shapes the entire race regardless of her finishing position.
runners_data.comment: Krissy won three starts back but managed only fourth two starts back and ninth on her latest outing, making her form hard to trust; she has run over today's trip and returns after 32 days, though her speed rating of 67 hints she may need to find more.

runners_data.name: Polygram
runners_data.note: In-form filly whose two most recent runs produced a win and a second, and her trainer Davidson has had one winner from six in the last fortnight; genuinely a hold-up performer who finds herself mapped to midfield only because the rear of the field is saturated with similar types — treat her chance as contingent on getting a clear run from further back than she'd ideally want.
runners_data.comment: Polygram ran a fine second last time out and was a winner two starts back, showing she knows how to find the line, and her experience over today's trip and going only strengthens her claims from stall one; the question is whether 136 lb blunts her finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Porth Eilian
runners_data.note: Bethell's three-year-old has form figures of 1-3-1-3-4 at distances up to a mile, so this step up to 1m1f on Good to Soft is the key question; a natural hold-up performer who will need room to be produced, and Rodriguez has the course knowledge to manage the Hamilton home straight well.
runners_data.comment: Porth Eilian arrives on the back of a win two starts back and a third last time out, with a trainer firing at 36% over the past fortnight and a speed rating that underlines her claims; the main risk is whether 31 days off leaves her just short of peak sharpness.

runners_data.name: Foxy Night
runners_data.note: Consistent performer whose recent runs have nearly all been thirds and seconds at shorter trips on Flat and AW; headgear note applies, and Egan is an astute pilot who may hunt an opening on the outside rather than get buried on the rail with several other hold-up types — the trip slightly longer than ideal based on history.
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in her last five starts without a win, Foxy Night brings solid recent form to the table, and 21 days since her last run suggests she arrives fresh; the 134 lb burden, however, makes life harder from stall two.

runners_data.name: Thankfully
runners_data.note: Won on Soft ground last time out, which is directly relevant here, and her trainer Burke fires horses fit from breaks; having been pulled up or finished well beaten in three prior runs before that win, the form profile is volatile, but the going form stands out in a field where not everyone has proven soft-ground ability.
runners_data.comment: Thankfully ran over today's trip and going and boasts a rating of 92 that marks her out as the one they all have to beat in this field; the concern is her recent string of disappointing efforts, with three successive poor runs to overcome from draw 6 carrying 133 lb.

runners_data.name: Wild Dahlia
runners_data.note: Haggas-trained three-year-old with a win and a second over seven and eight furlongs on good-to-firm and standard, so this Good to Soft is a potential concern; a natural prominent racer who should travel just behind Krissy, and Fallon will look to take closer order than her stablemates might manage — headgear noted.
runners_data.comment: Wild Dahlia arrives here in fine recent nick, third last time out and a winner three starts back, with experience over today's trip and going working in her favour; the 131 lb she carries is the one query, but at 23 days fresh she should strip fit.

runners_data.name: Sharona
runners_data.note: Off 401 days and returning for Bedi's small string after a layoff; her historical form is almost entirely over marathon distances of 16 furlongs and upward, meaning this 1m1f trip is sharply shorter than her comfort zone — a natural hold-up type squeezed into the midfield map position, but the combination of a long absence and unsuitable trip makes her chance reliant on everything going right.
runners_data.comment: A lengthy absence of 401 days and a bottom ranking on our figures make Sharona hard to fancy, though she has run over today's distance and going before, and that win three starts back shows she can find the track on her day.

runners_data.name: Second Fiddle
runners_data.note: A tough, consistent seven-year-old who has placed in each of her last six starts, never winning; ran only 10 days ago for Jardine and has the fitness edge — a genuine prominent type who should slot in just behind the lead and grind out a solid effort if the pace is moderate, though her win-less run of form is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Second Fiddle has nonetheless shown consistency with a string of minor placings, and she has run over today's trip and going before; at 127 lb from stall seven, however, she faces a stiff task against better-rated rivals.

runners_data.name: Saxon Grace
runners_data.note: Hat-trick winner for the small Bourke yard — four wins from four runners in the last 14 days is a hot streak — and she ran just six days ago so fitness is obvious; a prominent racer by style who will want to be forward, and her rapidly ascending form on Good and Good to Soft ground makes her the most interesting watch in the field even though her OR of 59 means she is conceding weight to most rivals.
runners_data.comment: Saxon Grace has winning form — a winner last time out and victorious in two of her last three starts — and has run over today's trip and going before, but she ranks eighth of nine on our figures and her speed rating of 53 makes her difficult to fancy at the weights.

races.paceDynamic: Krissy is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and, with no credible challenger for the lead, she will be allowed to bowl along at her own rhythm from the gates on Good To Soft Hamilton ground over a mile and one furlong. Behind her, Wild Dahlia and Second Fiddle are the natural prominent types likely to track close, while Saxon Grace — in sharp form having won three of her last four — will also want to be handy and could push for a position just behind the pace. The redistribution note is important here: Polygram and Sharona are genuine hold-up performers who have been bumped to midfield on the map because the rear of the field is overcrowded with natural hold-up types — Porth Eilian, Foxy Night, and Thankfully also want to come from off the pace, meaning there is a genuine late-race traffic problem waiting to unfold. With Krissy likely to control an honest but unforced tempo on softish ground, this race shape most clearly favours prominent racers able to travel close to the pace without expending energy early, as they will be best placed to capitalise if the hold-up contingent finds room too late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Krissy Controls, Handy Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Krissy dictates an uncontested front-running tempo and the hold-up pack is left with too much to do in the home straight.
scenarios.body: Krissy sets a sustainable rhythm that stretches the field on the uphill Hamilton finish, leaving prominent trackers Wild Dahlia and Saxon Grace perfectly poised to pounce at the two-furlong pole without having to find an extra gear from deep; the Good To Soft surface rewards those who travel within themselves through the race rather than those who must produce a sustained late run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Folds, Late Closers Arrive
scenarios.trigger: If Krissy goes too hard early and ties up in the closing stages, opening the door for the hold-up group.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected early gallop burns off Krissy and compromises the prominent racers, leaving a late lane for Porth Eilian or Thankfully — both of whom have won at similar trips on testing ground — to sweep through.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos, Wide Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the overcrowded hold-up group gets boxed in on the rail and one horse is forced wide but finds clear air.
scenarios.body: With five horses all wanting to come from off the pace, the rail becomes congested turning for home, and the horse that has the nous or room to go around the outside gets a clear run while others are checked; Foxy Night with David Egan's positional intelligence or Polygram — though naturally further back than shown — could be the beneficiary.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Saxon Grace Wire To Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Saxon Grace, fresh from a hat-trick of wins, is ridden more aggressively than expected and disputes or challenges Krissy from the outset.
scenarios.body: A second front-runner joining Krissy would create a genuine two-horse battle for the lead, making the pace hot enough to cause attrition throughout the field; Saxon Grace's hat-trick form is on Good to Good-Soft and she has the class to sustain it if allowed an unchallenged front position herself.

watchPoints.text: Krissy is uncontested on the front end but has a poor record on similar going (0W 0P from 15 runs) — watch whether she maintains a genuine gallop or idles, as any variance in tempo directly changes every scenario probability.

Saxon Grace arrives on a hat-trick having run six days ago — if Bourke's hot yard sends her forward aggressively from stall six, she could create a two-horse battle for the lead that pressurises Krissy and materially alters the pace shape.

Five horses — Polygram, Porth Eilian, Foxy Night, Thankfully, and Sharona — all want to come from rear or midfield, creating a real risk of rail congestion entering the final two furlongs; any horse drawn wide or ridden wide by its jockey gains a significant positional advantage.

Sharona's 401-day absence combined with a trip drastically shorter than her proven distance range (16f+) makes her an outsider with serious logistical concerns — monitor market moves as a proxy for whether connections have schooled her specifically for this type of race.

Good to Soft is the declared going for this race at Hamilton; Thankfully's win on Soft last time and Foxy Night's one placing on similar ground are the standout going-form credentials in the hold-up group, worth noting if the ground rides on the slower end of the description.

races.name: Darley EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Nakassama
runners_data.note: Five-time Hamilton runner with a deeply encouraging record at this track (1W, 4P), including wins and places over comparable distances on good and soft ground — the course form is a genuine asset, and Shane Gray knows this horse well; a natural hold-up operator sitting last of three before unleashing late, with solid similar-going figures (10/15 runs, 1W 4P) underpinning stamina credentials.

runners_data.name: Flagbearer
runners_data.note: A Haggas/Fallon combination with an OR of 120 commands respect on paper, but this three-year-old has run just once (4th, 8f, good) and steps up substantially in trip to 1m3f on soft ground — the lightly-raced profile and unknown style (tagged U) mean class may not fully translate, and Fallon will need to find a position in a three-runner field without natural pace rivals to track.

runners_data.name: Lord d'Or
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race, Andrew Balding's three-year-old has a consistent placed record (four seconds from his last four starts) and will lead without a challenger — the soft going at Hamilton is the key unknown, but his 32-day absence is not alarming, and Rodriguez is well-suited to front-running rides; the uncontested lead over 1m3f is his primary weapon.

races.paceDynamic: Lord d'Or is the sole confirmed front-runner and will lead from the outset, setting a controlled, uncontested tempo over 1m3f on good-to-soft ground at Hamilton. With no rival willing or able to challenge for the lead, Callum Rodriguez can dictate terms at whatever rhythm suits his mount, which in soft-ish conditions over this trip will likely mean a measured gallop that conserves energy into the straight. Flagbearer (style unknown, lightly raced) and Nakassama sit in behind, with the latter a genuine hold-up operator whose five-run Hamilton history shows consistent finishing from off the pace. This race shape — a lone leader controlling tempo, small field, soft ground — strongly favours a horse that can either make all unchallenged or, conversely, a hold-up finisher with enough class to reel in a front-runner who has had it too easy; the critical question is whether Lord d'Or's controlled lead gives him an unassailable advantage or leaves him vulnerable to a single, well-timed run from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lord d'Or Makes All
scenarios.trigger: If Lord d'Or dictates an uncontested, well-judged tempo and kicks clear before challengers can organise.
scenarios.body: Rodriguez engineers a perfect front-running ride, using the small field and lack of pace pressure to control the race from flag to finish without burning energy; the soft ground rewards a horse that travels economically rather than one forced to make ground. A small field with no pace rival means no one forces the issue, and Lord d'Or's consistent placed record (four consecutive seconds) suggests he is a reliable front-runner who knows how to see out a finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Nakassama Lands Late Blow
scenarios.trigger: If Lord d'Or sets a pace that is just slow enough to appear unwinnable but Shane Gray times a powerful hold-up run to perfection in the straight.
scenarios.body: Nakassama's Hamilton record is compelling — 1 win and 4 places from 5 visits, including course victories at extended distances on soft-ish ground — and a hold-up horse on a track it knows well is dangerous even against a controlling front-runner. With only three runners, Gray needs to judge the gap correctly in the straight, and if Lord d'Or's lead flatters only to deceive, Nakassama's proven staying ability on this course gives it a genuine shot.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Flagbearer Announces Class
scenarios.trigger: If Flagbearer's OR=120 represents a massive class advantage and Cieren Fallon produces it with a well-timed challenge from a prominent position.
scenarios.body: Flagbearer is a Haggas-trained, Fallon-ridden three-year-old with a 120 Official Rating — comprehensively the highest-rated runner in this field — and if that class translates over a trip and ground it is untested on, it could sweep past everything.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Soft-Ground Affair
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground proves more testing than the good-to-soft official reading and no runner handles conditions convincingly.
scenarios.body: A slower, energy-sapping surface could unsettle Lord d'Or's rhythm and blunt Nakassama's finishing kick, creating a messy contest decided by the horse that handles the ground best rather than by pace shape or class.

watchPoints.text: Lord d'Or's tempo — if Rodriguez allows too slow a gallop unchallenged, he could leave Nakassama with an easy target to reel in up Hamilton's straight.
Flagbearer's trip and ground experience are both untested — if the soft ground proves taxing, the highest-rated horse in the field may not fire at all.

Nakassama's 23-day turnaround is fine, but at OR=82 it faces a 38-point class gap to Flagbearer; if that rating is accurate, the hold-up run may simply not be good enough regardless of tactical execution.
Hamilton's uphill finish suits resolute stayers — with only three runners and soft ground, the final 2f will be the decisive phase and any horse short of peak fitness could be exposed.

races.name: Scullion Law Lanark Silver Bell Handicap Stakes (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: El Burhan
runners_data.note: Won on Soft at 10f and has course-stamina form; Pat Cosgrave is a positive booking, and the prominent style suits this pace shape perfectly — the main concern is whether 1m4f at Hamilton on this ground stretches his stamina beyond his best.|
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and a winner four starts back, El Burhan arrives here on a tight 15-day turnaround in fair recent nick, with experience over today's trip and going in his favour; the 140 lb burden is the one query, but his profile makes him hard to oppose.

runners_data.name: Yabher
runners_data.note: William Haggas yard in good form (7/38 T14) but Yabher's two wins came on Good and the soft-ground form string shows a distant 12th; a true hold-up horse who needs cover and a strong pace to unleash — neither is guaranteed here.|
runners_data.comment: Yabher won two of his last five starts and returns on a sound 24-day break, with experience of both today's trip and conditions working in his favour; the main concern is that his two most recent runs have both ended in unplaced efforts.

runners_data.name: Strassia
runners_data.note: 330 days off the track is a significant flag, but David O'Meara returns horses fit and the soft-ground credentials are outstanding — two wins, three places from ten runs on similar going; a true hold-up type who genuinely needs the gallop to stretch.|

runners_data.name: Noble Horizon
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose last five runs have all been on Good ground at shorter; steps up in trip for a yard with modest recent stats (0/2 T14) and the going step-up here is untested — needs to prove he handles it.|
runners_data.comment: Noble Horizon won two starts back and was runner-up last time out, showing solid recent form, though a seventh three starts back tempers expectations; he rates close to the official mark of 97 and steps in 24 days ago looking fresh enough.

runners_data.name: Teumessias Fox
runners_data.note: 63 days since last run and a P (pulled up) in recent form is concerning; hold-up style needs a strong gallop to fire, which this pace map does not guarantee, and the soft going has historically found him out.|
runners_data.comment: Teumessian Fox shaped with clear promise when third three starts back, and his rating of 105 gives him strong claims here despite being winless in recent starts; the main risk is that pulled-up effort last time out, now 63 days ago, leaves his current fitness in the balance.

runners_data.name: Lavender Hill Mob
runners_data.note: Form figures of 8-14-6-8-6 in the last five tell their own story; runs in headgear over marathon trips and has placed form on Soft, but needs a truly severe gallop over further than this to get competitive.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Lavender Hill Mob does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and 13 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh, though his recent finishes make improvement essential off a mark of 91.

runners_data.name: Spioradalta
runners_data.note: Three wins and three places from ten runs at 10-12f; prominent style suits the expected race shape and recent 2nd over 12f on Good is encouraging, but the absence of any soft-ground form in the data warrants monitoring.|
runners_data.comment: Rated well below the principals on our figures and ranked 11 of 15, Spioradalta is hard to fancy on bare merit, though he does own experience over today's trip and going, and a runner-up finish last time out at least suggests he arrives in reasonable nick after 34 days off.

runners_data.name: Evanesco
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner; Charlie Johnston's 3yo has won at 10f and can make all without a pace rival — the key question is whether his stamina extends to 1m4f on Good to Soft, as all five recent runs have been at a mile.|
runners_data.comment: Evanesco catches the eye on his third-place finish last time out, and a winner four starts back shows he can find the front end; he has experience of today's going and our rating puts him right in contention. The worry is a patchy recent run of form that will need to straighten out here.

runners_data.name: Salamanca City
runners_data.note: Won four of his last five starts including back-to-back wins on Soft; prominent style, soft-ground proven, and James Fanshawe's yard is ticking (5/22 T14) — sits in an excellent tactical position to track Evanesco and pounce.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom tier of this field on our figures and her speed rating of 80 gives little encouragement, but Salamanca City arrives in fine heart with three wins in her last five starts, has experience of today's distance and going, and 34 days between runs looks a fresh enough preparation.

runners_data.name: Ashnak
runners_data.note: Placed second on Soft (13f) and third on Good over 12f; David O'Meara has him primed (8/52 T14) and the prominent style suits a race where space behind the leader is available — the step up to 1m4f is a slight query.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Ashnak at least showed promise with a second two runs back, but a seventh last time out is harder to forgive; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 127 lb, and our rating of 92 leaves him with something to prove from the middle of this field.

runners_data.name: Evaluation
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with all his best form at 16f-plus on Good to Soft; mapped to midfield because the field has an excess of back-markers — he may struggle to get his true position and his chance is tempered accordingly, though the form figures over further are solid.|
runners_data.comment: Showed a win and a second in recent starts but has been unplaced in his last two outings, and 310 days off the track is a significant fitness query; has run over today's trip and going, and his rating of 94 offers some encouragement, though the layoff is the key concern.

runners_data.name: Altareq
runners_data.note: Has shown a tendency to race prominently in recent outings despite a natural hold-up style; mapped to midfield because the genuine closers outnumber available rear slots — his best form (win at 8f, 3rd at 8f) is on Good and shorter than today's 1m4f.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom but one on our figures and winless in his last five starts, Altareq faces a stiff ask, though he does boast a win three starts back and a third four starts back to show he can find the frame when conditions suit.

runners_data.name: Elsass
runners_data.note: Won twice at 11f on Good, but both recent efforts in soft-ish conditions have produced modest finishes; a natural hold-up type carried forward on the map — the trip and the going are questions, and racing out of role reduces the upside.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked well adrift of this field on our figures, Elsass is hard to fancy off a seventh last time out, though he does bring distance and going experience to the table and his two wins in his last five starts show he retains ability when conditions click.

runners_data.name: Tiernan
runners_data.note: Won at 11f on Good and placed at 10f; all of his placed form is on Good ground and the step to Soft at 1m4f is a significant unknown — sits in the midfield cluster because true hold-up territory is congested, which compromises his preferred style.|
runners_data.comment: Tiernan won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but his recent record also includes two unplaced efforts in his last five starts, and an official mark of 85 leaves him with something to prove against potentially higher-rated rivals.

runners_data.name: Letsbefrank
runners_data.note: Amie Waugh (3) claims, which helps the weight, and Letsbefrank has won twice at 11-17f on Good with a placed run on Soft; only 5 days since the last run is worth noting — a genuine hold-up horse nudged forward on the map because the back is full.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Letsbefrank is hard to fancy at these weights, though he does return just five days after winning last time out, has run over today's trip and going before, and his recent record shows three wins in his last five starts.

races.paceDynamic: Evanesco is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in a field of 15 over 1m4f on Good to Soft at Hamilton, David Egan can dictate a controlled, energy-conserving gallop from the front. The prominent types — El Burhan, Noble Horizon, Spioradalta, Salamanca City and Ashnak — will settle in behind but none has the profile or incentive to force a pace duel, meaning Evanesco is likely to be uncontested and able to set exactly the fractions he wants. Several of the field's true hold-up horses (Evaluation, Altareq, Elsass, Tiernan, Letsbefrank) have been redistributed to midfield on the map because there is insufficient room at the rear for all of them; in practice the field holds more hold-up types than can realistically sit last, and Altareq and Letsbefrank — who have both raced prominently in recent runs — are among those likeliest to be forced forward of their natural position. The race shape firmly favours horses that can travel prominently, sit just off a controlled pace, and quicken from the front two furlongs out rather than horses dependent on a strong gallop to reel leaders in late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Evanesco Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Evanesco leads without pressure and sets a measured pace that suits prominent stalkers over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Egan dictates the tempo throughout, with the prominent pack unable to close down a horse rationing his effort on Good to Soft; the last quarter-mile becomes a test of stamina-in-hand rather than a sprint, and those sitting closest to the leader benefit most.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Evanesco's lead is sustainable but one of the prominent hunters travels powerfully and swoops in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A horse like Salamanca City or El Burhan, who have both won on Soft and are proven over this kind of trip, tracks the leader and moves upsides from two out as the gallop consolidates; the decisive factor is the ability to quicken on softish ground rather than raw acceleration.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Runner Weaves Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough to string out the field and a genuine hold-up type finds gaps in the straight.
scenarios.body: Strassia, a proven Soft-ground handler with strong form at this trip and longer, has the profile to arrive late if the leaders do enough; Ashnak, with soft-ground placed form, could also thread through from midfield if daylight appears.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the displaced hold-up horses (Altareq, Letsbefrank, Tiernan) are pushed forward and one adapts well enough to outrun the field.
scenarios.body: Racing out of their preferred style reduces their chance materially, and this scenario relies on a pace collapse that forces everyone wide open; Letsbefrank's recent form and stamina give it the best outside chance of the redistributed group if circumstances conspire.

watchPoints.text: Evanesco (front-runner) must be watched for stamina; if he shortens stride entering the home straight at Hamilton, the race opens dramatically for the prominent pack behind him.|

Salamanca City is proven on Soft and in back-to-back winning form — if Daniel Muscutt gets a clean passage tracking Evanesco from the second fence, he becomes a serious danger irrespective of scenario.|

Strassia returns from 330 days off and her soft-ground credentials are outstanding over this trip and beyond — watch for early signs of rustiness in the preliminaries; if she moves freely she could be underestimated.|

The cluster of redistributed hold-up types (Evaluation, Tiernan, Letsbefrank, Altareq, Elsass) may produce a scramble for position in the first two furlongs — watch for interference or horses being shuffled further back than intended, which could compromise their already-limited chance.|

Noble Horizon is unproven on going softer than Good and steps up significantly in trip; if the ground is riding genuinely testing by the time this race runs, watch for early signs of struggling to maintain the prominent position he needs.|

races.name: Acrisure Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Germanic
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with two wins at 5-6f and good trainer form (1 from 21 in 14 days is competitive); on similar going has placed twice in 15 attempts but is 0W, suggesting a tendency to find one too good — Ryan Sexton looks for a prominent pitch and the 5f trip suits.
runners_data.comment: Germanic bounced back to win two starts back and arrives here fit on 24 days' absence, with experience of today's trip and going working in his favour and a rating of 93 underlining his claims — though a cold trainer strike-rate of 5% over the last fortnight is the one note of caution.

runners_data.name: Advertised
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a 1W-0P record in 8 sim-going runs; only 69 days off is a concern, Grant Tuer's 14-day form is positive (1/10), and while all recent wins came at 7f on Good, a drop to 5f on soft is an untested combination that makes assessment difficult.

runners_data.name: Sir Yoshi
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose sim-going record (0W0P from 15) is a significant negative; placed third at 5f on Good recently but has run 9th twice at the trip — David Nolan will need everything to fall right from the rear on a track where Hamilton rarely gives late closers a free run.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Sir Yoshi does at least offer a third two starts back as encouragement, and he has run over today's trip before; however, ninth finishes either side of that placed effort suggest consistency remains an issue at a stiff 139 lb from stall 13.

runners_data.name: Sturlasson
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who has won on Soft (1W1P from 4 sim-going runs) giving him a clear going edge over most rivals; Cieren Fallon is an excellent booking and the 75-day absence is a mild flag, but this horse has enough soft-ground evidence to be taken seriously from off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Sturlasson ran a solid second three starts back but has been winless in his last five, and 75 days off the track adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, and his 137 lb burden from stall 10 makes life no easier.

runners_data.name: Stargazed
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and ran just two days ago, which is a major fitness concern even for a handler as active as K.R. Burke (8/32 in 14 days); prominent style fits the race shape but the sim-going record (1W1P from 9) is modest and the quick turnaround makes this a risky runner to trust.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Stargazed faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's trip and going before and our figures rate her well clear of her official mark at 95 — draw four and 134 lb the key questions after a run just two days ago.

runners_data.name: Canon's House
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner, confirmed leader for Michael & David Easterby; Joanna Mason is an experienced pilot around Hamilton and the horse's record at 5f on Good-adjacent ground (1W2P from 15) is workmanlike — uncontested lead is the asset here, not raw ability.

runners_data.name: Parisiac
runners_data.note: Carries genuine soft-ground form (2W7P from 15 sim-going runs, including two wins and a 2nd on Soft) and is naturally a prominent racer by inclination; however, with the prominent slots congested, he is likely to be shuffled into midfield against his instincts, which will blunt his effectiveness — treat any chance with appropriate caution.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well outside the leading assessments in a field of thirteen, Parisiac is hard to fancy off an unplaced last effort 46 days ago, though he has run over today's trip and going before and that second from two starts back shows he retains ability when conditions suit.

runners_data.name: Oriental Prince
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse by style and history, Jim Goldie's yard is in form (4/38) but this horse's sim-going record (0W0P from 15) is poor; placed 2nd at 5f on Good but that is a lone bright spot — the redistribution note is secondary to the fact that the form profile on this surface is simply weak.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 12 of 13 on our figures, Oriental Prince faces a stiff ask here, though he was second last time out and has run over today's trip and going before, and 20 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh enough.

runners_data.name: Justmyluck
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type who ran only six days ago; Linda Perratt's 14-day return (2/15) is modest, the sim-going record is 0W0P from 10, and the weight is light at 119lbs — the quick return and weak going form make this a difficult runner to support.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and winless in his last five starts, Justmyluck faces a stiff ask at the weights carrying 119 lb from stall one, though he has run over today's distance and going before and that sole recent win shows ability is there somewhere.

runners_data.name: Tatterstall
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Michael Dods whose recent form includes a 2nd and 3rd at 5f on Good, showing he is in reasonable fettle; Daniel Muscutt is a polished jockey who can find a position in behind the leader, but the sim-going win rate (0W from 15) suggests he typically ends up just missing — value in a placed position rather than a winning one.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Tatterstall nonetheless showed ability with a second and a third in that spell, though two unplaced efforts — including most recently, 24 days ago — temper confidence; he has run over today's distance and going before and carries 137 lb from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Vantheman
runners_data.note: Tom Eaves partners a consistent prominent type for Kevin Ryan who won at 5f on Good earlier this season; wears blinkers, which keeps him focused, and the trip and style both fit the anticipated race shape — 0W from 15 on sim-going is the fly in the ointment.

runners_data.name: Jordan Electrics
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up veteran trained by Jim Goldie who won at 6f on Good earlier in the season; the wears a hood (hg:p) and has placed on Soft before, but 0W from 15 on sim-going and an age-related stamina question at 5f on soft ground limits optimism — the sharp 5f Hamilton track is not ideal for genuine closers.
runners_data.comment: Jordan Electrics bounced back to win last time out, though that followed an eighth three starts back that raises questions about consistency; he has run over today's trip and going, but 136 lb from stall 12 is no gimme.

runners_data.name: Eternal Sunshine
runners_data.note: A naturally prominent type whose best recent efforts came at 5f on Good (2nd twice); Lauren Young is an inexperienced 5lb claimer, and with the prominent spots already spoken for by higher-OR rivals, Eternal Sunshine is likely to end up racing out of position — the style-fit discount and OR of 84 combine to make this a difficult winner to construct.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked tenth of thirteen on our figures, Eternal Sunshine faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's trip and going before and her two placed efforts in recent form suggest she retains some ability.

races.paceDynamic: Canon's House is the sole confirmed front-runner and should lead from the gates at Hamilton's sharp 5f, setting a genuine but uncontested pace on Good to Soft ground. Behind her, Germanic, Advertised, Stargazed, Tatterstall, and Vantheman form a cluster of prominent types who will jostle for the early positions in behind, creating natural pressure on the leading group without anyone likely to seriously challenge Canon's House for the front. The hold-up horses — Sturlasson, Sir Yoshi, Justmyluck, and Jordan Electrics — will be forced wide or to the rear, giving ground away on a track where Hamilton's uphill finish rewards those who conserve energy early rather than burn it fighting for position. This field contains more prominent types than can realistically slot in behind the leader — Eternal Sunshine and Parisiac are genuine prominent racers by inclination but are likely to find themselves shuffled into midfield, racing out of their natural role, which reduces their effectiveness. The tactical verdict is clear: a controlled, uncontested lead for Canon's House sets up a race shape that favours prominent horses travelling smoothly in second or third who can capitalise on a steady early gallop, with true hold-up horses having to find an improbable late surge up the hill.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Canon's House Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Canon's House leads unchallenged and the prominent pack behind ride their horses without triggering a breakneck gallop
scenarios.body: Canon's House dictates a measured pace, conserving enough to kick clear inside the final furlong on softened ground; prominent types tracking her in second and third have the ideal launch pad on Hamilton's uphill finish

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Poachers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent quartet travelling smoothly in behind delivers a perfectly timed run to collar Canon's House in the final 100 yards
scenarios.body: A prominent horse like Germanic or Tatterstall, tracking the leader without burning petrol, quickens past an exposed Canon's House who has done too much work; the Good to Soft ground rewards those who wait just a fraction longer

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Storm Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace from Canon's House and the chasing pack proves genuine enough to set up a strong finish for hold-up horses off the bend
scenarios.body: Sturlasson or Jordan Electrics, dropped in behind early, gets a clear run up the stands rail and finishes powerfully past tired rivals who fought for position; the soft underfoot conditions amplify stamina and close down speed horses in the final 100 yards

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Blunts The Favourite
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent cluster becomes fractious early, causing multiple horses to race keenly and burn out before the straight
scenarios.body: The scramble for position in behind Canon's House produces an unusually fast early pace that collapses the field entering the final furlong; a lightly-raced or freshened runner on the outer benefits from a clean passage as rivals fold

watchPoints.text: Canon's House faces no genuine front-running rival — if Joanna Mason controls the fractions cleanly, the race is run entirely to this horse's strengths and the entire field is chasing her shadow.

Stargazed ran only two days ago — monitor market moves and any trainer comment; if there is any residual fatigue from a quick turnaround, a prominent horse travelling on the bridle in behind could collapse late and mislead punters about the true pace.

The congested prominent group of Germanic, Advertised, Tatterstall, and Vantheman could cause early jostling for second and third — any horse that gets bumped or checked losing two lengths on this sharp 5f course will have very little time to recover.

Sturlasson's soft-ground winning record stands out in a field dominated by Good-ground specialists — if the Going to Soft stamp on this race proves genuinely testing, his form profile becomes markedly more relevant than his odds might suggest.

Jim Goldie runs three horses (Parisiac, Oriental Prince, Eternal Sunshine) — watch for any stable runner that attracts disproportionate market support, as it may signal which of the three Goldie's team expects to perform best on the day.

races.name: Patersons Of Greenoakhill Handicap Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Hunky Dory
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner, gets a free lead here on soft ground where she has shown some form (1W from limited similar-going starts); however, a 2-day turnaround is short and her recent record reads 518636, suggesting consistency issues — the solo lead is a major asset but she's not guaranteed to capitalise.|
runners_data.comment: Hunky Dory brings a third two starts back and a win five starts back to recommend him, and has run over today's trip and going, with 140 lb from stall seven the main query after a return just two days ago.

runners_data.name: Sir Garfield
runners_data.note: Won twice on good ground at 6f and has a 7-day freshen-up behind him; David Nolan is a strong booking and he's placed once from four similar-going starts, hinting the step into softer conditions may just blunt his sharpest form slightly — nonetheless his natural prominent style is perfectly suited to this race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Sir Garfield shaped well when second last time out, returning quickly after just seven days, and has run over today's trip and going before; the main risk is that his two efforts prior to that placed finish were modest, suggesting consistency remains a question.

runners_data.name: Lipsink
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who has won at this trip on standard and good ground, but a 70-day absence is a significant concern; runs in a hood and is placed from two similar-going starts with one win, suggesting he handles the surface — Michael Appleby's 2/18 strike rate in the 14-day window is modest, so fitness must be queried.|
runners_data.comment: Lipsink won three of his last five starts but hasn't raced for 70 days, which queries fitness, and a second last time out at least shows he retains some form; he has experience over today's trip and going, and carries 138 lb from stall eight.

runners_data.name: Abduction
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse who gets his natural position here; best form has come over 7f on good ground and all five recent runs have been at 7f or further — this 6f on soft looks a combination of too short and too testing, and his record of 773332 suggests he finds more to beat than he beats.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent without a win in recent starts, Abduction has been placed in four of his last six outings, including second last time out and third two starts back, and returns after 25 days with experience of today's trip and going on his side, though converting that consistency into success remains the challenge.

runners_data.name: Stirrup Cup
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type who won over 6f on soft, making him relevant if closers get a chance — but in this race he's been pushed into a midfield position he doesn't naturally occupy, which compromises that form profile; 65-day break adds a fitness query on top of the tactical problem.|
runners_data.comment: Stirrup Cup won two starts back but could only finish fifth last time out, and 65 days off the track is a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, and carries 133 lb from stall one, though our rating of 76 suggests he holds a small edge over his mark.

runners_data.name: Ashen
runners_data.note: Has strong form at 6f on good-to-soft adjacent conditions (placed twice from two similar-going runs) and is lightly weighted — but he's a natural prominent racer who can't get that berth in this field, meaning he'll have to produce his best from an unfamiliar middle-pack position that materially undermines his chance.|
runners_data.comment: Ashen ran second last time out and second three starts back, but the unplaced effort two starts back drags on confidence, and ranked tenth of eleven on our figures he faces a stiff ask at these weights despite having run over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Kisses
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up horse who is placed once from just one similar-going start with no wins; 13-day turnaround is fine, but her form on soft (14th of 14 at 6f last time similar going) is a red flag — she's also unable to settle as deep as she'd prefer given the redistribution, compounding the challenge.|
runners_data.comment: Whiskey Kisses is winless in her last six starts, and ranked last on our figures, making her hard to fancy despite carrying a manageable 120 lb from stall 10; the consolation is she has run over today's trip before and arrives on a sharp 13-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Jannas Journey
runners_data.note: Rhys Elliott apprentice claim (5lb) is a potential asset but Janna's Journey's form is at 7f-8f on good ground — this 6f on soft represents a sharp drop in trip and a surface step-up simultaneously, and a 13-day turnaround follows a ninth-place finish; Jim Goldie's 4/38 T14 rate is unremarkable.|
runners_data.comment: Jannas Journey won three starts back but has struggled since, finishing ninth last time out, and while she has run over today's distance and going before, a mark of 78 and 138 lb make improvement hard to find from stall three.

runners_data.name: Wreck It Ryley
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and Cieren Fallon is an excellent spare booking; his best soft-ground placing was a 3rd over 6f but the wider record (838963) suggests a horse who is hit-and-miss — Alan Brown's 0/6 T14 strike rate offers no stable form to lean on, and 23 days since last run is neutral.|
runners_data.comment: Wreck It Ryley returns in good time after 23 days, brings both distance and going experience to the table, and his third last time out is the sharpest recent form in the field, with our rating of 84 marking him out as the one to beat despite being winless in his last six.

runners_data.name: Belsito
runners_data.note: Has the best soft-going form record in the field numerically (2W4P from 15 similar-going starts) and wears a hood; Tom Eaves rides, Kevin Ryan's stable is a reliable outfit, and he's a natural prominent type who should get his position — the 25-day break is fine, though his most recent SOF run was 8th.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked ninth of eleven on our figures and with a trainer in the depths of a miserable run — just one winner from 24 in the last fortnight — Belsito is hard to fancy at the weights, though a win two starts back and distance-and-going experience count in his favour.

runners_data.name: Shoot To Kill
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who prefers 7f-8f based on all recent runs yet drops to 6f here; a genuine prominent racer who cannot secure that position in this field and must race from midfield instead — his style-fit is the lowest in the race at 0.94 and his form at the trip and going combo is limited.|
runners_data.comment: Shoot To Kill shaped with plenty of promise when third two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, with an 82 rating suggesting he's better than his official mark of 74 — the risk is he's winless in his last six and needs to find a career best.

races.paceDynamic: Hunky Dory is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she should be allowed to stride into a comfortable position from the outset and control tempo on soft ground over six furlongs at Hamilton. Sir Garfield, Lipsink, and Belsito are the natural prominent types likely to track her in the first rank, creating a sustainable, measured gallop rather than a contested burn — that dynamic typically rewards horses who can hold a handy position without expending excess energy early. The field carries more pace than the map can accommodate: Ashen and Shoot To Kill are genuine prominent types but are likely to find themselves shuffled into a midfield position they don't naturally favour, while Stirrup Cup and Whiskey Kisses are true hold-up horses similarly unable to settle as far back as they'd prefer. This race shape — a solo front-runner setting a controlled tempo on soft turf — overwhelmingly favours prominent racers who can sit just off Hunky Dory and pounce, with hold-up horses facing a particularly stiff task if the pace is never truly end-to-end.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Hunky Dory dictates an honest but uncontested gallop and the race is won by a horse tracking within two lengths.
scenarios.body: Hunky Dory sets a regulated pace that suits those holding a position just behind her, with the soft ground ensuring the gallop is genuine enough to expose any horse who idles; a horse like Sir Garfield or Lipsink, travelling comfortably in the slipstream, picks up approaching the final furlong and powers past.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Leader Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Hunky Dory meets minimal friction and the gallop is insufficient to stop her sustaining the run to the line.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing to pressurise her early, Hunky Dory benefits from a dawdle that dulls the finish and plays to her lead-and-stay profile; on soft ground she may simply never be caught if the tempo is falsely slow.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Emerge
scenarios.trigger: If the early fractions are stronger than expected and the prominent group burns out, allowing runners from deeper to get involved.
scenarios.body: Should Lipsink or Sir Garfield push Hunky Dory harder than anticipated, the pace becomes genuinely testing on soft ground and horses like Abduction or Wreck It Ryley — true hold-up types getting their natural position — can close late; however, this scenario is constrained by the fact that Stirrup Cup and Whiskey Kisses, nominally the deep closers, are not genuinely settled at the rear in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Out-Of-Role Winners
scenarios.trigger: If the race breaks down in traffic, pace horses are hampered, and a redistributed runner lands the race from an unnatural position.
scenarios.body: Ashen or Shoot To Kill, unable to secure their preferred prominent berth, have to race from midfield but get a dream passage through; this is a low-probability shape because both are explicitly racing out of role and their style-fit discount is significant.

watchPoints.text: Watch Hunky Dory's early behaviour — if she jumps cleanly and goes unchallenged to the lead, the whole race is set around her; any stumble or slow break fundamentally changes the shape of this race.|

Ashen and Shoot To Kill are both natural prominent types who may attempt to push forward from the gate despite the redistribution — if they do press Hunky Dory, the pace sharpens and the scenario shifts away from Scenario A toward Scenario C.|

Lipsink's 70-day absence is a significant unknown on soft ground for a nine-year-old — if he shows any sign of needing the run early, the prominent group behind Hunky Dory thins and the race becomes more compressed.|

Monitor Stirrup Cup's draw and early positioning — a genuine soft-ground winner at this trip who would be dangerous if he can get further back than his redistribution suggests, but in this shape he is unlikely to find the cover he needs to produce his best finish.|

Belsito's soft-going form record (2W4P) stands out across the field — if his hood has the desired effect and he travels comfortably tracking the pace, his experience on this surface makes him a consistent player regardless of how the race unfolds.|

races.name: Patersons Of Greenoakhill Handicap Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: Winged Messenger
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed pace-setter who has won on soft over 6f at Hamilton, giving him a meaningful course-and-conditions profile; racing from a prominent style that suits today's shape well, though a 56-day absence for Julie Camacho's yard (1 from 21 in 14 days) is worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Winged Messenger's winning effort four starts back, combined with experience over today's trip and going and a rating of 88 that ranks him second in this field, makes him a genuine threat from stall seven carrying 140 lb; the concern is a trainer firing at just 5% in the last 14 days.

runners_data.name: City Captain
runners_data.note: 104-day absence is the major query, but Harriet Bethell's 1/8 14-day record suggests the horse is fit to go; two soft-ground placed efforts over 6f in the form string and Rodriguez booked is an encouraging combination for a prominent runner who should sit nicely in second or third.
runners_data.comment: City Captain won one from five in recent starts and has run over today's trip and going, yet his last outing — a fourth — came 104 days ago, and that absence is the key question mark; the 138 lb burden does him no favours either.

runners_data.name: Montezuma
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's runner returns quickly after 14 days and steps up from 5f to 6f, where his one run at the trip in the recent form string produced a distant 13th, raising a distance question; races prominently and the soft ground at Hamilton is familiar territory, but the trip remains to be proven.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Montezuma does offer some encouragement — a second and a third in recent outings suggest he is competitive, though a fifth last time out tempers optimism; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 138 lb from stall four keeps him squarely in the mix.

runners_data.name: Miraculous
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby sends this horse out quickly after 15 days with David Allan up; a genuine hold-up horse whose natural style has been mapped to midfield as the field is loaded with closers, meaning he is unlikely to get a clear, late sight of the race — his single soft-ground placing came at Southwell Fibresand which is an unreliable comparator.
runners_data.comment: Miraculous showed what he is capable of when winning last time out, but that eight-place finish two starts back is a reminder of his inconsistency; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 134 lb from stall ten keeps things honest.

runners_data.name: Dandy Magic
runners_data.note: Won on good ground over 6f recently to give Goldie a double interest in the race, but that win came as a hold-up horse with room to finish; pushed into a midfield slot by the congested hold-up group, so Lauren Young's claim is a minor positive but the compromised position is a significant negative on a day when pace is not strong.
runners_data.comment: Dandy Magic won last time out, which catches the eye, but she ranks ninth of ten on our figures and faces a stiff ask from stall nine carrying 134 lb; the distance and going hold no fears at least.

runners_data.name: Daizen
runners_data.note: A winner over this course and distance on good ground, Cieren Fallon takes over for Rebecca Menzies whose yard has produced 0 winners from 6 runners in the last 14 days; the 46-day break and patchy recent form (including a 16th on debut) temper expectations despite the tactical positional advantage.
runners_data.comment: Daizen has won in his last five starts but the other four runs are unplaced or fifth, and ranked eighth of ten on our figures he faces a stiff ask here; he has run over today's trip and going, and 46 days between runs is a manageable absence.

runners_data.name: Iris Dancer
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old veteran with wins over this course and distance, Iris Dancer is a true closer whose last six runs have been on good ground and who is mapped forward of his natural position due to the density of hold-up types in this field; Andrew Mullen knows the horse but the headgear (blinkers) and 10-day turnaround for Tristan Davidson's small yard are the key tactical flags.
runners_data.comment: Iris Dancer has finished ninth and unplaced in her last two starts, making her hard to fancy as the lowest-rated runner in the field, though she does bring distance and going experience and a fresh enough pitch just ten days after her latest outing.

runners_data.name: Lord Bertie
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse who fades in the finish, with nine of his last 15 runs producing double-figure finishes on going soft or slower; David O'Meara's 8/52 14-day record is active, but a hold-up style on a day with no searching pace and a tendency to weaken late makes this a difficult race to win.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Lord Bertie nonetheless catches the eye as the top-rated runner here, and his experience over today's trip and going counts in his favour; drawn in stall one carrying 138 lb, a return to form at 28 days fresh is needed but he sets the standard.

runners_data.name: Wobwobwob
runners_data.note: Carries the fades-in-finish flag and a deeply unimpressive soft-ground record showing two placings from 10 attempts in those conditions; the 70-day break, veteran status at eight years old, and visor headgear suggest connections are hoping for a career-best on unsuitable terms — the race shape does not help.
runners_data.comment: Wobwobwob has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 81 gives him a case as a leading danger at the weights, yet his winless recent spell — unplaced three times in his last five — makes a turnaround essential after 70 days off.

runners_data.name: They All Know Me
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's runner has a soft-ground win over 7f at York and is stepping back to 6f with David Nolan in the saddle; a genuine hold-up type who may find the 6f too sharp in a slowly-run race, but soft-ground form is solid and the step down in trip could sharpen up a horse whose recent form shows a drop-off.
runners_data.comment: They All Know Me landed a win three starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, with his our rating of 79 suggesting he retains ability; the chief concern is back-to-back unplaced efforts since that victory.

races.paceDynamic: Winged Messenger is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to press him, is set to bowl along at a sustainable gallop on soft ground over 6f at Hamilton. City Captain, Montezuma, and Daizen will track closely in the prominent slots, meaning the leading group will be three to four wide and organised from the outset, but none of them are likely to put Winged Messenger under serious early pressure. The field contains more hold-up types than the map can place at the rear — Miraculous, Dandy Magic, and Iris Dancer are true closers who will likely be shuffled into midfield rather than their natural deep position, compromising their finishing kick. On this pace shape — a single, unhurried front-runner setting a moderate to steady tempo over soft ground — prominent racers who can travel just off the pace and sustain their effort through the final furlong are best placed, with genuine hold-up horses at a tactical disadvantage given the lack of searching early pace to set up a late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Winged Messenger Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Winged Messenger travels comfortably to the front unchallenged and sets a moderate pace that suits his stamina on soft ground.
scenarios.body: Winged Messenger dictates every yard, conserving energy through the first half before kicking on from two out; the soft going rewards his demonstrated ability to see out 6f in these conditions, having won on soft at this course previously. Prominent horses sitting just behind can challenge but are unlikely to reel in a horse who has dictated on his own terms, especially given he has a soft-ground win over this course and distance.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Overpowers
scenarios.trigger: If one of City Captain or Montezuma travels powerfully in Winged Messenger's slipstream and produces a sustained challenge from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: City Captain arrives on the back of soft-ground experience over 6f and with Callum Rodriguez in the saddle brings strong tactical awareness to chase down a front-runner who has been given a soft lead; Montezuma's proven ability in soft-adjacent conditions gives Jim Goldie's runner a live chance if the tempo quickens sufficiently to bring his prominence into play.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Runner Finishes Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong and a horse from the middle division threads through tiring rivals.
scenarios.body: A moderate gallop can still produce late gaps on soft ground if the leaders tie up, allowing a horse like Dandy Magic or Miraculous — both genuine hold-up types shuffled forward into midfield — to benefit from the race coming back to them; however, their compromised starting position reduces the probability of getting a clean, late run as they would naturally prefer.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Attrition Test
scenarios.trigger: If the ground rides genuinely testing and the race becomes a stamina grind that turns the final furlong into a war of attrition.
scenarios.body: Horses who have already demonstrated soft-ground resilience over 6f come to the fore, and any runner who has been forced wide or used energy early will drop away; Lord Bertie and Wobwobwob, both flagged as fading types, are at maximum disadvantage here, while They All Know Me's soft-ground win at 7f hints at stamina that could be unlocked.

watchPoints.text: Winged Messenger sets the pace entirely alone — watch whether he is allowed to dictate at a canter or whether City Captain and Daizen push him into a stronger gallop in the first two furlongs, as that decision determines the entire race shape.

Montezuma steps up to 6f having been beaten 13 lengths over the trip on his only previous attempt at the distance — if he struggles to see it out, Jim Goldie's second runner Dandy Magic could inherit a better position than expected.

Lord Bertie and Wobwobwob both carry the fades-in-finish flag and are hold-up types in a race with no pace to chase — both could be prominent dangers for the first four furlongs before emptying late and causing interference for runners behind them.

Three genuine hold-up horses — Miraculous, Dandy Magic, Iris Dancer — are mapped into midfield and will likely be closer to the pace than their connections intend; watch the draw and early positioning at the start to see if any can find a gap quickly enough to race closer to their natural style.

races.name: Hemmings Homes 10th Anniversary Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Jm Jhingree
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 5f on Good and has Good To Soft form in the book, but sim-going record is thin (3 runs, no wins or places on similar ground); true hold-up style in a race where that position is structurally crowded, and four days since last run is a tight turnaround to assess freshness.
runners_data.comment: Jm Jhingree landed a win in his last six starts and has experience over today's trip and conditions, with a third two starts further back adding solid recent form, though back-to-back unplaced efforts including a ninth last time out on just four days' rest are the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Thistle Nil
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Soft and has placed on similar going, giving it the best soft-ground credentials of the closers; however, the fades-in-finish flag is a serious concern on 5f Good To Soft where every yard counts late, and 39 days off means fitness is not guaranteed.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Thistle Nil has been unplaced in three of his last four starts, and his sole recent win came three starts back, making him hard to fancy despite having run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: King Of The Jungle
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner and the axis around which the entire race shape is built; won twice this season including on Soft and Good To Soft at 5f, but the STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) signals it is racing slightly out of its absolute comfort zone — nonetheless, uncontested lead is a powerful structural advantage here.
runners_data.comment: King Of The Jungle returns after 62 days off having won twice in his last five starts, most recently back-to-back victories, and he has experience over today's trip and going; however, carrying 139 lb and ranked sixth of thirteen on ratings gives him plenty to find against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Hi Lord
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up runner with solid 5f form including a win and two places over the trip on Good; the 7f/Soft run in recent history shows it handles ease in the ground, and Conor Whiteley's 5lb claim is a useful weight aid, though the crowded rear-group limits its ability to find clear running.
runners_data.comment: Hi Lord shaped well for third two starts back and got off the mark five starts back, so he arrives with some recent encouragement, returning quickly on 13 days' rest having run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Never Dark
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old hold-up specialist whose true nature is masked by redistribution into midfield — it is being pushed forward by sheer volume of closers in this field; sim-going record shows just one place from 15 similar-going runs, making it hard to fancy on current evidence regardless of position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Never Dark at least brings distance and going experience to the table, and a runner-up finish last time out — just 10 days ago — suggests he returns in decent nick; the 131 lb burden from stall 12 may test his resolve against stronger-rated rivals.

runners_data.name: Supremissy
runners_data.note: The finish-fade warning combined with a STYLE_FIT discount tells a consistent story — this filly is a hold-up type who will be shuffled forward against preference, and her soft-ground record (only one soft run, unknown finish) adds opacity; Andrew Mullen is a capable pilot but the horse's profile does not suit the likely race shape.
runners_data.comment: Supremissy has been largely out of the picture in recent starts, finishing ninth last time out and ninth four starts back, and an unseated rider also blights her recent record; our figures rank her tenth of thirteen in this field. Her win two starts back at least shows ability, and she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Falcon Queen
runners_data.note: Tom Eaves takes the ride on this 3-year-old whose recent form figures (4-8-6-9-8) tell a bleak story regardless of going; pushed out of her natural hold-up berth by the crowded rear group, she faces the double jeopardy of an uncomfortable position and zero sim-going wins or places from eight runs.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Falcon Queen arrives on a sharp 13-day turnaround having run over today's trip before, and her rating of 60 offers a sliver of hope, though a fourth being her best recent finish suggests she has plenty to find ranked ninth of thirteen.

runners_data.name: Doon The Glen
runners_data.note: Handles soft (won over 6f on Good, placed on Soft) and has visor headgear to sharpen focus; Jim Goldie's yard is in decent form (4/38 over 14 days) and Lauren Young's 5lb claim helps offset a modest OR of 50 — a genuine hold-up type who could benefit if the pace does collapse, though redistribution means she won't get the ground she wants.
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, Doon The Glen has finished fifth, seventh, and eighth in his last three starts, making him hard to fancy despite a win four starts back; he has run over today's trip and going before, but that experience does little to offset a deeply modest recent profile.

runners_data.name: Kyber Crystal
runners_data.note: A 7-year-old prominent racer wearing tongue-tie and cheekpieces, returning after 43 days off with a trainer showing 0 wins from 6 over the past fortnight; all five recent runs on Good ground suggest soft may be untested territory, and a sim-going record of one win from 15 runs on similar surfaces gives little comfort.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with a string of fifths her best recent efforts, Kyber Crystal faces a stiff ask from stall 11 carrying 124 lb, and ranked 11 of 13 on our figures; experience over today's trip and going is the one thread of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Harb
runners_data.note: Solid 5f form with multiple top-five finishes, but sim-going record is just one run and no wins or places — soft ground is a genuine unknown; as a redistributed hold-up type being mapped to midfield, Jack Garritty will need to decide whether to commit forward or drop back, and that tactical confusion is a risk in itself.
runners_data.comment: Harb arrives here 13 days fresh, has run over today's trip and going, and a third four starts back shows he can find the frame; however, he is winless in his last six starts, and carrying 135 lb from stall 5 leaves him with plenty to do at a mark of 60.

runners_data.name: Tanjen
runners_data.note: David Allan is a key positive — he's a top-level jockey on a horse that won over 5f on Good here at Hamilton; prominent style suits this race shape well and he's lightly exposed at 5f, but only one place from two similar-going runs suggests the eased conditions may blunt his zip.
runners_data.comment: Tanjen won last time out and returns just 10 days later in fine heart, with experience of both today's trip and going working in her favour; the concern is that carrying 135 lb from stall seven represents a stiff ask against a strong field.

runners_data.name: Impressor
runners_data.note: A 9-year-old hold-up type wearing a visor, with a mixed soft-going record (wins and places over 6f on Soft, but mostly Good performers) and 13 days since last run; Sam James is a solid booking but Impressor's recent form figures (0-0-6-3-6-0) suggest he is well below his best, and the style mismatch in this race shape is an additional hurdle.
runners_data.comment: Impressor is rated highest of all 13 runners here and has experience over today's distance and going, making him a leading danger despite being winless in recent starts; the main concern is an unplaced effort last time out just 13 days ago, which leaves something to prove on current form.

runners_data.name: Startling
runners_data.note: The most consistent horse in the race with five consecutive top-four finishes and a second over 5f on Soft; prominent style is a perfect structural fit for this race shape, the blinkers should maintain focus, and the one question is whether Startling can finally convert its serial placing form into a win.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Startling has nonetheless shown admirable consistency with four runner-up finishes in that sequence, and she has run over today's trip before; carrying 135 lb from stall eight, her rating of 65 offers some encouragement, though a first win remains elusive.

races.paceDynamic: King Of The Jungle is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 13-runner field and, on Good To Soft ground at Hamilton, is likely to bowl along at a sustainable pace without being seriously pressured for the lead — Tanjen, Kyber Crystal and Startling will push up prominently but none is a natural pace-setter who will force King Of The Jungle into an unsustainable gallop. The going report confirms the 8:15 race is Good To Soft, easing conditions that will reward horses with stamina reserves and penalise those who burn energy early, meaning even a moderate pace here carries more sting late than it would on a quick surface. Behind the prominent group, the bulk of this field — Harb, Supremissy, Never Dark, Falcon Queen, Doon The Glen, Jm Jhingree, Thistle Nil, Hi Lord and Impressor — are natural hold-up types, but with so many closers chasing so few positions at the rear, several will be forced to race closer to the pace than they would prefer. This race shape — a single front-runner setting a measured pace on soft ground with a crowded midfield — strongly favours horses who can travel prominently in second or third, getting cover without expending early energy, then sustaining their effort through the final furlong; pure hold-up horses relying on a strong pace collapse are at a structural disadvantage given King Of The Jungle is unlikely to be run off its feet. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear; Harb, Supremissy and Never Dark are the most likely to be pushed forward out of their preferred position, with Doon The Glen and Falcon Queen the ones most likely to genuinely settle away from the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: King Of Jungle Controls
scenarios.trigger: If King Of The Jungle leads uncontested and sets a fair but manageable tempo on the Good To Soft, staying prominent throughout.
scenarios.body: King Of The Jungle has won twice this season including over 5f on soft, and Joanna Mason will exploit the absence of genuine pace rivals to dictate terms; the Good To Soft surface rewards its preference for prominent racing without asking for a scorching early gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Holds On Late
scenarios.trigger: If Tanjen or Startling tracks King Of The Jungle closely in second or third and produces a sustained run from two out.
scenarios.body: On Good To Soft ground the front two or three home positions rarely get run down in a sprint unless the early pace is extreme, and Startling's habitual second-place finishes suggest it knows how to conserve and sustain; Tanjen won over this course and distance and has the tactical pace to sit just off the leader and pick up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Gets Lucky Break
scenarios.trigger: If King Of The Jungle sets an unexpectedly strong pace and ties itself up inside the final furlong, allowing a hold-up horse to reel it in.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires a pace collapse that the current race shape does not clearly point to, but Hi Lord has solid placed form at 5f on soft and Doon The Glen handles soft and has won over longer trips suggesting stamina; both are genuine hold-up types who could benefit if the pace does collapse.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Falls Apart Entirely
scenarios.trigger: If the crowded midfield creates interference and the race becomes chaotic, allowing a completely unconsidered runner to emerge late.
scenarios.body: The redistribution of multiple natural hold-up types into midfield creates the possibility of positional jostling and interference that disrupts the race shape unpredictably; Impressor has soft-ground placed form and Jm Jhingree won last time out over this distance, meaning either could benefit from a messy race that nullifies the prominent runners' advantage.

watchPoints.text: Watch King Of The Jungle's opening furlong — if it bowls along unchallenged, the race may effectively be over early; any horse looking to challenge should ideally be within a length or two turning for home.

Harb, Supremissy and Never Dark are natural hold-up types likely to be pushed into unfamiliar midfield positions at the start — watch for crowding and potential interference between the 3f and 2f markers as these horses try to find gaps.

Thistle Nil carries a finish-fade flag on just 5f — if it tracks the pace prominently it risks emptying inside the final furlong; watch whether Rhys Elliott drops it out or tries to race up with the pace, as either decision carries risk.

Startling's pattern of consecutive second-place finishes deserves attention — if it travels smoothly in third or fourth heading into the final furlong, it has a habit of running to a reliable level and could be the value lurking in the prominent group.

Going confirmation is Good To Soft (not Soft as listed in race conditions) — horses whose form is specifically on Soft rather than Good To Soft may not get the conditions they truly need, worth checking any horse with a strong soft-only preference.
